trajectory.thought: The leader is the median of the full pool (a seed baseline), and the verdict is "indistinguishable" — the runner-up is not statistically better. Given the series has a strong trend with moderate seasonality, the top models are all in one correlated-error group, and only 3 validation windows make weight estimation high-variance, the robust median is the right choice. The catastrophic outliers in the tail models (788B error) are handled well by the median, and no subset or weighting strategy has shown a statistically meaningful improvement.

action_args.justification: The series is strongly trend-dominated (trend strength 0.98) with moderate seasonality (0.40) and non-stationary. The top 8 models are all in one correlated-error group (12 of 19 models share errors), so combining them adds little diversity. The tail models carry catastrophic outliers (worst error ~788B), which the median naturally discards. With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights are high-variance and the ranking is only moderately stable (Kendall tau 0.55). The median of the full pool is robust to both the outlier tail and the correlated top group, and no alternative strategy achieved a statistically distinguishable improvement over it.
